description: Na₈SnSi₆O₁₈ crystallizes in the trigonal R̅3m space group. There are three inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a body-centered cubic geometry to eight O atoms. There are four shorter (2.64 Å) and four longer (2.68 Å) Na-O bond lengths. In the second Na site, Na is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted NaO₆ octahedra that share corners with six equivalent SiO₄ tetrahedra, faces with three equivalent NaO₈ hexagonal bipyramids, and  a faceface with one SnO₆ octahedra. There are three shorter (2.28 Å) and three longer (2.52 Å) Na-O bond lengths. In the third Na site, Na is bonded to eight O atoms to form NaO₈ hexagonal bipyramids that share corners with four equivalent NaO₈ hexagonal bipyramids, corners with two equivalent SiO₄ tetrahedra, edges with two equivalent SnO₆ octahedra, edges with four equivalent SiO₄ tetrahedra, and faces with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.32-2.73 Å. Sn is bonded to six equivalent O atoms to form SnO₆ octahedra that share corners with six equivalent SiO₄ tetrahedra, edges with six equivalent NaO₈ hexagonal bipyramids, and faces with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra. All Sn-O bond lengths are 2.08 Å. Si is bonded to four O atoms to form SiO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one NaO₈ hexagonal bipyramid,  a cornercorner with one SnO₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent SiO₄ tetrahedra, and edges with two equivalent NaO₈ hexagonal bipyramids. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 36-50°. There are a spread of Si-O bond distances ranging from 1.59-1.67 Å. There are three inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to three Na, one Sn, and one Si atom. In the second O site, O is bonded to three Na and two equivalent Si atoms to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing ONa₃Si₂ trigonal bipyramids. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to four Na and one Si atom.
